references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the demon-possessed man who met Jesus when he landed in the country of the Gerasenes. Matthew mentions two demon-possessed men coming from the tombs.

Mark's parallel account of the demon-possessed man in the country of the Gerasenes who lived among the tombs, could not be bound, and cried out night and day. Mark gives a more detailed description of the man's condition.
The preceding verse that tells how Jesus and his disciples sailed over to the country of the Gerasenes, providing the geographical context for the meeting with the demon-possessed man.
Describes further how the unclean spirit had seized the man many times, and though he was bound with chains and shackles on his feet, he broke them loose, which elaborates on the man's condition.
After the healing, the formerly demon-possessed man sits clothed and in his right mind, a contrast to the condition described in Luke 8:27 where he had no clothes on him.
Isaiah describes people who sit among the tombs and spend the night in secret places, which recalls the demon-possessed man's dwelling among the tombstones.
